page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized compute instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The system offers 64.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a high memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions cover AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. This instance configuration omits local storage and contains no GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highmem-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, ranking in the top 25 percent. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench (multi-core score of 6622.0), and PassMark CPU tests falls within the average range. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 62.15 GB/sec for large-block reads and 39.95 GB/sec for writes. Specialized benchmark results show static web serving throughput of 10.63 GB/sec and Redis SET performance at 8.97 million operations per second. LLM prompt processing performance is average for small 135M models at 607.92 tokens/sec, but drops to weak relative performance for 7B models at 18.65 tokens/sec.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with strong single-threaded CPU throughput renders this server suitable for memory-intensive enterprise tasks, in-memory caching, database management, web serving, and software compilation. Tradeoffs include the total absence of local NVMe SSD storage, requiring reliance on network storage for persistence, as well as limited efficacy for medium-to-large language model inference due to missing GPU hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is an x86_64 compute instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 cores, and 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating with a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, it features 32 MB L3 cache alongside instruction extensions like AVX, AES, and FMA. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU throughput alongside average multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance. In practical application tests, it delivers 10.63 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 8.97 million Redis SET operations per second. The server lacks attached local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on persistent remote storage solutions. These hardware specifications position the instance for memory-heavy enterprise tasks, in-memory caching layers, software compilation, and moderate data analytics workloads.
